ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Two skateboards, A and B, of equal height with masses of $1\mathrm{kg}$ and $2\mathrm{kg}$ respectively, are on a smooth horizontal surface. Blocks C and D, each with a mass of $1\mathrm{kg}$, are placed on the right end of A and the left end of B, respectively. A and C move to the right with the same velocity $v_{0}=10\mathrm{m/s}$, and B and D move to the left with the same velocity $kv_{0}$. At some moment, a collision occurs, with a very short interaction time. After the collision, C and D stick together forming a new block, and A and B stick together forming a new skateboard. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the blocks and the skateboards is $\mu=0.1$. The magnitude of the acceleration due to gravity is taken as $g=10\mathrm{m/s}^{2}$.

1. If $0<k<0.5$, determine the magnitude and direction of the velocity of the new block CD immediately after the collision.
2. If $0<k<0.5$, determine the magnitude and direction of the velocity of the new skateboard AB immediately after the collision.
3. If $k=0.5$, calculate the magnitude of the relative displacement between the new block and the new skateboard from the moment of the collision until they reach relative rest.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$v_{CD}=5(1-k)\mathrm{m/s}$, direction to the right
$v_{AB}=\frac{10-20k}{3}\mathrm{m/s}$, direction to the right
$1.875\mathrm{m}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, two skateboards are on the same horizontal plane, the left one is skateboard A, and the right one is skateboard B; small block C is placed above the right end of A, and small block D is placed above the left end of B. The upper surfaces of the two skateboards are at the same height, so when the left and right two groups move toward each other and meet, the upper C and D will collide and stick together, and the lower A and B will collide and stick together. Then reason: Take the direction to the right as the positive direction. The collision action time is extremely short, and the friction impulse between the blocks and the skateboards during the collision is ignored. 1. Use conservation of momentum separately for the upper C and D. The initial velocity of C is +v0=+10 m/s, and the initial velocity of D is -kv0=-10k m/s; the masses of both are 1 kg, and after the collision they stick into CD: v_CD = [1×10 + 1×(-10k)]/(1+1) = 5(1-k) m/s. When 0<k<0.5, 5(1-k)>0, so the direction is to the right. 2. Use conservation of momentum separately for the lower A and B. The mass of A is 1 kg, and its initial velocity is +10 m/s; the mass of B is 2 kg, and its initial velocity is -10k m/s; after the collision they stick into AB: v_AB = [1×10 + 2×(-10k)]/(1+2) = (10-20k)/3 m/s. When 0<k<0.5, 10-20k>0, so the direction is to the right. 3. When k=0.5, immediately after the collision: v_CD = 5(1-0.5)=2.5 m/s, v_AB = (10-20×0.5)/3=0. After this, CD slides to the right relative to AB, and friction hinders the relative motion of CD. The mass of CD is 2 kg, and the mass of AB is 3 kg. The normal force is N=2g=20 N, and the kinetic friction force f=μN=0.1×20=2 N. For CD: a_CD = -f/2 = -1 m/s^2. For AB: a_AB = f/3 = 2/3 m/s^2. The relative acceleration a_rel = a_CD - a_AB = -1 - 2/3 = -5/3 m/s^2, and the initial relative velocity v_rel0=2.5 m/s. When relatively at rest, v_rel=0; from 0 = v_rel0^2 + 2 a_rel s: 0 = 2.5^2 - 2×(5/3)s, s = 1.875 m.

v_CD = [1×10 + 1×(-10k)]/(1+1) = 5(1-k) m/s.

v_AB = [1×10 + 2×(-10k)]/(1+2) = (10-20k)/3 m/s.
When 0<k<0.5, 10-20k>0, so the direction is to the right.

3. When k=0.5, immediately after the collision:
v_CD = 5(1-0.5)=2.5 m/s,
v_AB = (10-20×0.5)/3=0.

When relatively at rest, v_rel=0; from 0 = v_rel0^2 + 2 a_rel s:
0 = 2.5^2 - 2×(5/3)s,
s = 1.875 m.
